children: Peru's economy grew 3.56% in July from a year earlier, official data showed on Tuesday, beating expectations as strong gains in construction, trade and services offset weakness in manufacturing, agriculture and fishing.
The reading from INEI, Peru's statistics agency, accelerated from 1.75% growth in June.
Construction jumped 9.85% and trade rose 6.79%, helping drive the expansion. The mining and hydrocarbons sector, a cornerstone of Peru's economy, was nearly flat but still positive, edging up 0.24%.

By contrast, manufacturing, agriculture and fishing contracted. Fishing posted the steepest drop, down 27.44%, after a collapse in anchovy catches. INEI said industrial anchovy fishing was almost entirely wiped out.
